title: Donovan's Conjecture over Algebraically Closed Fields
main_claim: Fix a prime p, an algebraically closed field K of characteristic p, and a bound M. Then blocks of finite group algebras KG whose defect groups have order at most M fall into only finitely many K-linear Morita equivalence classes. This is Donovan's conjecture over K for all finite p-groups, including nonabelian ones and p=2. The proof has two parts. The first is a uniform Cartan bound for quasisimple blocks of bounded defect (Sections 2-6). The second is a reduction to crossed extensions, finished off by a Sylow-equivariant Frobenius comparison (Sections 7-8). The result is then transferred from F_p-bar to K.

issues.description: The finiteness of the integral base orders, and of their Picard images, depends entirely on two cited results: EEL Theorem 3.10 (bounded Cartan sum, defect and integral Morita-Frobenius number give finitely many O-Morita classes) and Eisele's Theorem B / Corollary 1.2 (finite integral Picard groups of blocks over W(k)). I could not check the exact hypotheses of these from the sources available here. The argument is correct if both apply as stated.
issues.evidence: "Eaton--Eisele--Livesey, Theorem~3.10 \cite{EEL}, says precisely that bounded Cartan sum, bounded numerical defect ... and bounded integral Morita--Frobenius number give finitely many integral Morita classes."

issues.description: The fixed-root-data Cartan bound rests on two claims: the summed Ext estimate is independent of |(A_x)_p| (via the change of variable to the covering torus), and the tilting-type objects have standard flags of uniformly bounded length. I spot-checked these but did not fully verify them. Their correctness depends on Eteve's construction and on equivariant descent details I could not check line by line. I did not identify a specific failing step.
issues.evidence: "The covering torus has the same dimension as T. Therefore the total dimension of this constant complex is 2^{rk T}, independent of |(A_x)_p|."
